claim_being_audited: The model can be certified for deployment based on aggregate launch readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, despite an unresolved multilingual customer-support weakness, because monitoring and rollback planning are sufficient support.
decision_criteria: If admissible evidence showed the multilingual weakness was resolved and no material limitation remained, certification could be compliant.
If admissible evidence showed an approved mitigation or risk acceptance with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion, caveated certification could be compliant.
Absent one of those showings, certifying the model while the model card says no known material limitations remains insufficiently supported under the stated policy.
evidence_requests: Provide an approved mitigation or risk-acceptance record covering the multilingual customer-support issue, including owner, alert threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
Provide updated model-card language explicitly disclosing the Spanish-language refund-guidance limitation for the named launch use case.
Provide evidence that the multilingual support slice has been remediated and now meets target, if claiming no material weakness remains.
Provide the final approval trail showing launch certification was conditioned with documented caveats, if that is the actual action being defended.
specific_concerns: Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support general readiness but do not satisfy the policy condition for certification without material caveats.
The unresolved weakness is still current and is concentrated in Spanish-language refund guidance for a named launch use case.
The mitigation artifact is only a draft runbook, with accountable owner and alert threshold still marked TBD.

The policy text requires either no remaining material weakness or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion; the available evidence does not show that standard is met.
The model-card draft states there are no known material limitations even though reviewer comments identify the multilingual issue, creating a disclosure gap under the stated policy.
Public guidance on model cards and AI risk management is relevant background, but it does not override the internal release-policy predicate.
unsupported_claims: That the model can be certified on the present record without first disclosing the material limitation or obtaining approved risk acceptance.
That a monitoring-and-rollback concept is enough to remove the current disclosure requirement.
That the evidence supports a clean certification decision rather than, at best, a caveated or deferred one pending policy-satisfying documentation.
